taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS's California blackberry review (Tirmenstein 1989, read 2026-10-15): "a low-growing ... native evergreen shrub".

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: FEIS's California blackberry review (Tirmenstein 1989, read 2026-10-15): "The somewhat prickly, deeply-lobed, alternate leaves".

traits.leaf_division.note: A model estimate (confidence high), FEIS (Tirmenstein 1989) calls the leaves deeply lobed and palmate; they are leaves of three leaflets.

traits.inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: FEIS's California blackberry review (Tirmenstein 1989, read 2026-10-15): "Perfect flowers ... develop in clusters of 2 to 15 near the ends of leafy branches".

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS's California blackberry review (Tirmenstein 1989, read 2026-10-15): "Aggregates of druplets, commonly referred to as 'berries'".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: FEIS's California blackberry review (Tirmenstein 1989, read 2026-10-15): fruit "oblong or conical, somewhat bristly, and up to 0.8 inches (2 cm) in length"; the 1 cm least is the model estimate's.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), FEIS gives only the trailing stems' 5-6 m length (Tirmenstein 1989); the mound's height is the model's.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS's California blackberry review (Tirmenstein 1989, read 2026-10-15): its phenology table: flowering April-June, fruit ripening June-August.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS's California blackberry review (Tirmenstein 1989, read 2026-10-15): its phenology table: fruit ripening June-August.

generator.params.note: Himalayan blackberry's values, changed by hand for trailing blackberry: a low mound of slender, wide-angled, drooping canes that trail along the ground (FEIS, Tirmenstein 1989: "low-growing ... or climbing", stems to 5-6 m long), fine prickles, three-parted leaves and small clusters of white flowers ripening to oblong black fruit. Weak apical dominance, wide-angled drooping canes and a short path_half make a low mound under 1 m, the species-facts estimate's greatest height. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: A mound 60 cm high at 12 years in the open, by eye from photographs of trailing stands. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: green canes turning brown (FEIS: "greenish when young but turn brown at maturity"); leaves paler beneath; white flowers; shiny black oblong fruit.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2989958), as no source read gives it.
